findings.text: Prototype pollution. `buildPath` never rejects `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype` path segments. A form field named `__proto__[polluted]` gives the path ['__proto__','polluted']. `obj['__proto__']` is `Object.prototype`, which is truthy and an object, so it is reused and `Object.prototype.polluted = value` is set globally. `constructor[prototype][x]` reaches the same place. Fix: skip these keys, for example `if (name === '__proto__') return true;`.

0.reason: `__proto__` matches `\w+`, so the path ['__proto__','polluted'] gets through. `obj['__proto__']` is Object.prototype, which is truthy and passes isObject, so it is reused, and the recursive buildPath then sets Object.prototype.polluted. That is prototype pollution, a different flaw from the reference bug about splitting names on non-word characters.
